title: Structured Inductive Bias for Multi-timescale Knowledge Tracing

problem.claim: Knowledge tracing must infer evolving cognitive states from interaction sequences while accounting for entangled long-term accumulation and short-term contextual fluctuations.

gap.claim: Most existing models treat different timescales as independent parallel feature channels, overlooking hierarchical co-evolution and potentially degrading generalization when learning evidence is limited.

contributions.claim: FSKT introduces an Experiential Learning Theory-based structured inductive bias to model the co-evolution of multi-timescale cognitive dynamics.

FSKT decomposes latent representations with a causal stationary wavelet transform and uses a cascaded architecture aligned with four ELT stages to order information flow across frequencies and stages.

FSKT uses geometric projection, residual stripping, and a weakly supervised sufficiency constraint to separate stage-specific semantics and align stage representations with observable learning signals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on five datasets showing competitive performance and more stable generalization under data sparsity and varying observed history lengths.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge tracing infers evolving learner cognitive states from interaction sequences to predict future performance.
Learning behavior is non-stationary and involves tightly entangled long-term and short-term dynamics.
Existing models commonly represent timescales as independent parallel channels, which overlooks hierarchical co-evolution and can harm sparse-data generalization.
FSKT combines wavelet-based frequency decomposition, ELT-aligned cascaded evolution, geometric projection, residual stripping, and a sufficiency constraint.
Experiments on five datasets are reported to show competitive performance and more stable generalization across sparse data and history lengths.

unknowns: The five datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not report ablations or isolate the effects of the individual architectural components.
The abstract does not provide details about the wavelet configuration, training procedure, or computational cost.
